looked_at.what: The lecturer begins defining KL divergence.
Cross entropy is recalled as attaining its minimum when p and q coincide.
The minimum cross entropy is identified as the entropy of p.
KL divergence is introduced as the difference between those two values.
The lecturer states that KL divergence is asymmetric.
The lecturer says the expression often appears in a more compact form.
The compact form is said to hide a difference between cross entropy and entropy.

steps.question: What does the transcript establish about the compact KL expression?
steps.answer_text: It is the difference between cross entropy and the entropy of p, and the order matters because KL divergence is asymmetric.
steps.why: At 1897.7–1921.5 the lecturer defines KL from the gap between cross entropy and its entropy-of-p minimum; at 1953.9–1962.3 he states the asymmetry; at 1967.2–1981.3 he describes the compact form.

steps.question: Why does a single compact-sum term contain p_i/q_i rather than q_i/p_i?
steps.answer_text: For index i, subtracting entropy from cross entropy gives -p_i log(q_i) - [-p_i log(p_i)] = p_i[log(p_i) - log(q_i)] = p_i log(p_i/q_i).
steps.why: The transcript identifies KL as cross entropy minus entropy of p at 1897.7–1921.5 and the compact form as that same difference at 1967.2–1981.3. The logarithm quotient rule is general mathematical knowledge.
